description: Plan then build a straight-street district from 1–8 distinct Meshy/Tripo buildings, each manufactured once and reused as separate editable instances. Includes road, pavements, spawn, daylight and camera in the shared Map SceneDocument. Optional owned PBR road/pavement maps; otherwise simple solid surfaces. Plan returns layout, provider-credit count and account quote without spending. Build requires a budget and returns a persistent job, then Map Studio link. Private work version requiring visual review; no automatic Community publication or game replacement.

budget.description: Required for paid concept/build: maximum GripForge credits OR subscription USD accepted. Use the quote funding currency: insufficient AI allowance falls back to GripForge credits for the whole new job, never both. Use plan.concept_quote for images, plan.quote for Meshy. Provider credits are separate.

buildings.description: Unique building definitions with distinct ids. Each new model is manufactured once.

concept.description: Owned PNG/JPEG/WebP revision for Meshy image-to-3D. At most 12 MiB. Mutually exclusive with source.

concepts.description: Coherent views of ONE building, front first, for Meshy multi-image-to-3D. Exclusive with concept/source. Review coherence before building.

delivery.description: Preserve an immutable full-detail source without provider remeshing, then prepare 1–3 independent LOD GLBs. Highest detail first, decreasing triangles and texture sizes. Default maxError=.001, lockBorder=true prioritizes detail and may exceed targets. For distant levels, explicitly allow e.g. maxError=.005/.01 and lockBorder=false after review. Shared metric fit and preserved PBR. No normal rebake, runtime LOD switching or inferred collision. Also works with source at no provider cost.

dimensions.description: Maximum footprint and height in metres. Uniform fit preserves proportions; actual dimensions are returned.

finish.description: Free deterministic repair of an owned source + delivery. All coordinates are Y-up metres AFTER the returned importTransform. Explicit oriented removal boxes (rotation XYZ radians), regular shutters (+Z outward, yaw radians) and railing paths (feet, vertical posts, supports slopes). Measure and review regions first. Applied AFTER each LOD simplification to keep thin parts straight. Textures outside cuts stay byte-identical; removed surfaces are not capped. Triangle targets remain soft. No AI auto-segmentation or collision repair.

look.description: Rendering look, separate from the game style: stylized (neutral) | painted | toon | anime | realistic | lowpoly | pixel. Old values (handpainted, cartoon, low_poly…) are read as aliases. Omit for the style default. Fills style when style is omitted; toon, anime and pixel add their phrase to the prompt.

meshQuality.description: Meshy 7.1 quality. Defaults standard geometry and 2K PBR. Multi-image supports standard/2k geometry only. Texture resolution is preserved during optimization. Read the updated quote.

provider.description: 3D provider pinned to this recipe, Meshy by default. Tripo v3.1 requires one reviewed concept (no multiview yet) and uses v3.5 PBR textures. No automatic paid provider fallback.

source.description: Reuse an owned static GLB revision instead of paying for this building. The source is never modified.

tripoQuality.description: Tripo-only quality; default detailed geometry and detailed textures. extreme requests 8K. Read the separate provider quote. Exclusive with Meshy meshQuality and source.

road.description: SceneMaterialOverride: color, roughness, metalness, map/normalMap/roughnessMap/metalnessMap as owned immutable SceneAssetRef, repeat:[u,v]. Validated by the shared Scene Engine.

sidewalk.description: SceneMaterialOverride: color, roughness, metalness, map/normalMap/roughnessMap/metalnessMap as owned immutable SceneAssetRef, repeat:[u,v]. Validated by the shared Scene Engine.

repetitions.description: Instances per definition, without additional model generation cost.

stage.description: Default plan is free and does not generate. Read its quote, then explicitly build.
